AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, copied verbatim in substance. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from `__init__` (the_lost_and_forgotten.py:34-36). The game applies it from MonsterModel.AfterAddedToRoom awaited by CombatManager.AfterCreatureAdded inside StartCombatInternal, i.e. after every creature is on the board and before Hook.BeforeCombatStart; the sim runs it at create_monsters (combat.py:134), before relics attach (combat.py:157-159), before belt potions register (combat.py:164-166), before the parity Niche HP roll (combat.py:152-153) and before hooks.on_combat_start (combat.py:208). Same observable today on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the four ported listeners on the reachable hooks (relics/ruined_helmet.py, relics/unsettling_lamp.py, relics/vambrace.py, relics/paels_legion.py) all gate on the player or on a non-null card and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card; (b) HP-roll inversion -- of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp, and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581); (c) roll ordering -- EXECUTED, `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` prints `the_lost  sticky-no-op   initial=DEBILITATING_SMOG (MoveState)`, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the constructor's first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. Rule 7: the four relic files and powers.py are cited by name here and are NOT all hashed by this record. As with its twin, TheLost.cs:31-34 does not await base.AfterAddedToRoom(); the base is a no-op (MonsterModel.cs:313-316) so nothing follows from that. C# passes `applier: null` (TheLost.cs:33) and the sim passes none; PossessStrengthPower's own record already verdicts that faithful.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: TheLost.cs:36-45 is a pure two-cycle with NO branch state: DEBILITATING_SMOG -> EYE_LASERS -> DEBILITATING_SMOG, initial DEBILITATING_SMOG. EXECUTED (`graphs`): the sim prints exactly that. No RandomBranchState, so bug class 6 / G1 cannot apply here either.

guards.what: DebilitatingSmogMove: steal 2 Strength, and the order of the two applications
guards.rationale: TheLost.cs:47-53: Apply<StrengthPower>(targets, -2, applier: Creature) then Apply<StrengthPower>(Creature, +2, applier: Creature). the_lost_and_forgotten.py:51-55 does the same two in the same order, and passes applier=self on the player-facing one -- which is load-bearing, because PossessStrengthPower's tracker keys on the applier being its owner (audit/records/power/possess_strength.json, guard on PossessStrengthPower.cs:37). DebilitatingSmogStrengthStealAmount is GetValueIfAscension(DeadlyEnemies, 2, 2) = 2 on both branches.

EyeLasersDamage GetValueIfAscension(DeadlyEnemies, 5, 4) = 4 and WithHitCount(2) against the `_eyeLasersRepeat = 2` const (TheLost.cs:19, :57); the sim's _EYE_LASERS_DMG = 4 / _EYE_LASERS_HITS = 2 and the intent Intent(ATTACK, damage=4, hits=2) match. The multi-hit loop question is the next guard.

monsters/base.py:107-118 `_execute_attack` fires before_attack, loops `hits` times through DamageCmd.deal and breaks when the player or the attacker is dead; then after_attack. C#'s AttackCommand.Execute (AttackCommand.cs:528-546) has the same two loop guards -- `if (Attacker.IsDead) break;` and an empty alive-target list -- and the sim's single target IS the player, so the two loops agree hit for hit. The one asymmetry is C#'s PRE-loop `if (Attacker.IsDead) return this;` (AttackCommand.cs:528-531), which also skips Hook.BeforeAttack; the sim has no such pre-guard. Unreachable for this unit and EXECUTED rather than asserted (rule 5): a sim monster can only take a turn while dead if `retained_after_death` is set (combat.py:292, :306), that flag is written only where hooks.should_remove_from_combat_after_death returns False (cmds.py:102-104, :200-202), and `grep -rn 'def should_remove_from_combat_after_death' sts2_rl/` returns exactly two sites -- the hook itself (hooks.py:603) and ReattachPower (powers.py:2338), which this monster never holds.

TheLostAndForgottenNormal.cs generates (TheLost, null) then (TheForgotten, null), RoomType.Monster; THE_LOST_AND_FORGOTTEN_NORMAL (the_lost_and_forgotten.py:107-110) is `[TheLost, TheForgotten]` in the same order, which fixes the enemy slot order and therefore the CombatId numbering the replay targets by.
